title: Machine Vision Academy
text:
Editor's Note
        Machine Vision  is not just Computer Vision or Image Processing alone;  it is much more. In our view, it is one of the most important engineering disciplines behind modern automation and the factories of the future. It brings together the full inspection chain as one engineered system: part handling and presentation, lighting, optics, sensors, image processing and the automated action that follows.
        Machine Vision is not a new discipline, but recent advances in software and computing power have given it a new reach. What once felt limited to careful inspection and measurement is now expanding into cognitive functions for automated equipment, opening up a new frontier for innovation in industrial automation. That shift is exciting, and it is one of the reasons this field continues to draw so much attention from engineers who want to build systems that are smarter, faster and more capable.
        At the same time, there is still a real shortage of engineers with the right training, and far too few academic courses cover Machine Vision as a complete engineering discipline rather than treating Computer Vision as the whole story. That gap matters. The mission of the Machine Vision Academy is to help close it by providing free, open and practical knowledge, together with course material that supports both self-learning and institutional teaching.
      Only free knowledge and open collaboration will carry us from today’s problems to tomorrow’s solutions.

title: About
text:
Machine Vision Academy is a community-driven initiative created by individuals who want to share practical knowledge and experience in machine vision, computer vision and artificial intelligence.
It is not a commercial organisation or a separate legal entity. It exists through the digital content, repositories and website maintained by its contributors. Those assets are intended to support education, strengthen access to technical knowledge and help public institutions deliver high-quality learning material.

title: About
text:
Our Mission
Our mission is to make machine vision knowledge freely accessible, technically rigorous and genuinely useful.
We believe that high-quality learning should be available to everyone who wants to build, teach or understand machine vision systems. We also believe that open knowledge is stronger when it is shared with care, reviewed with discipline and presented in a form that is practical for real engineering use.
“Knowledge grows when it is shared freely and used well.”
Machine Vision Academy exists to support that principle.

title: About
text:
History
Machine vision has become a core technology in automation, inspection and digital manufacturing. Across industry, the number of practical applications has grown faster than the number of engineers formally trained to design and support them.
Over many years, the contributors to Machine Vision Academy saw the same challenge repeated: strong demand for machine vision expertise, but too little accessible training material that was both technically sound and aligned with industrial practice.
In 2026, the contributors decided to turn that frustration into action. Machine Vision Academy began as a practical response: a commitment to build open, high-quality learning resources for machine vision engineering. It remains a work in progress, but the goal is clear — to help close the gap between industrial need and educational opportunity, and to make machine vision expertise more accessible to all who want to learn it.

Estimated time to complete: 21 hours

title: Machine Vision Advanced
text:
Learning outcomes

Design calibrated image-measurement systems with explicit distortion, coordinate-frame and uncertainty models.
Compare stereo, structured-light, time-of-flight and point-cloud methods against task-specific accuracy and surface constraints.
Apply robust feature matching, registration, tracking and geometric estimation to variable industrial scenes.
Integrate multi-camera systems with PLCs, robots and industrial networks while maintaining deterministic timing and traceability.
Plan measurement-system studies, sampling plans and acceptance evidence appropriate to production deployment.
Diagnose advanced imaging failures by separating optical, mechanical, sensor, calibration, algorithmic and integration causes.

title: Machine Vision Fundamentals
text:
Learning outcomes

Explain how illumination, optics, sensors, processing and decision logic interact as one engineered inspection chain.
Translate an inspection requirement into measurable imaging, resolution, contrast, timing and acceptance criteria.
Select basic lighting geometry, wavelength, lens, camera and interface options for representative industrial applications.
Construct deterministic preprocessing, segmentation, measurement and identification flows using established machine-vision methods.
Evaluate repeatability, false-accept risk, false-reject risk and cycle-time performance using representative production evidence.
Document, troubleshoot and communicate a complete machine-vision solution using traceable engineering assumptions and test results.
